0-northborough-road-common-driveway.name: 0 Northborough Road common driveway special permit
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.description: Special permit application to allow 15 feet of frontage on an 8-acre parcel to divide the land into two residential building lots served by a common driveway.
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a frontage variance on September 16, 2026, allowing a 15-foot Massachusetts Water Resources Authority easement to serve as frontage for two proposed residential lots on a common driveway. At the same meeting, the board accepted the applicant's withdrawal of its companion special permit application. The project must now seek subdivision approval from the Planning Board, as town counsel advised that an Approval Not Required plan cannot rely on a variance.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 16 to approve the frontage variance and accepted the withdrawal of the special permit.
A relative of the applicant spoke in favor of granting the variance, citing past town precedent for access through a water department right-of-way.

0-southville-road.name: 0 Southville Road apartment development
0-southville-road.description: Proposed construction of two apartment buildings and associated infrastructure at 0 Southville Road.
0-southville-road.status: The proposed 60-unit apartment development at 0 Southville Road remains under environmental review, with its Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit hearings continued by the Conservation Commission on October 8, 2026. The two-building project falls within the MBTA Communities zoning district, requiring at least six affordable units. The Affordable Housing Trust has also explored whether municipal subsidies could buy down additional affordable units, awaiting cost estimates from the developer.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on October 8, 2026, to continue the Notice of Intent and stormwater permit hearings while awaiting revised plans responding to peer review.

positions.body: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust
positions.detail: Reviewed the 60-unit concept in March 2026 and requested cost projections from the developer to see if town funds could subsidize units beyond the 10 percent required.

0-valley-road-trail.name: 0 Valley Road footbridge and trail
0-valley-road-trail.description: Proposed construction of a wooden boardwalk and trail connection on Southborough Open Land Foundation land off Valley Road.
0-valley-road-trail.status: The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions on July 29, 2026, allowing an Eagle Scout project to construct a wooden boardwalk and dirt trail on Southborough Open Land Foundation land at 0 Valley Road. Abutters opposed the application, raising concerns over traffic, parking along a narrow road, trespassing, and wetland disruption. With the public hearing closed and environmental conditions established, the project is cleared to proceed following the standard appeal window.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0-1 on July 29 to issue an Order of Conditions with standard and special conditions after confirming modern treated lumber poses no water toxicity risk.
Spoke in favor of the project on June 25, stating that the proposed boardwalk and trail support its mission to offer passive recreation.
Valley Road abutters opposed the trail, citing safety and congestion from parking on a narrow road, loss of privacy, trespassing into yards, and disturbance to wildlife.

1-overlook-drive-pool.name: 1 Overlook Drive swimming pool
1-overlook-drive-pool.description: Notice of Intent to construct an inground swimming pool, patio, and cabana within the wetland buffer zone at 1 Overlook Drive.
1-overlook-drive-pool.status: The project is approved. On October 8, 2026, the Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to close the hearing and issue an Order of Conditions for the pool, patio, and cabana. Approval is subject to special conditions requiring eight native shrubs to be maintained in perpetuity and a pre-construction site visit to review machinery access protections.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on October 8, 2026, to approve the Order of Conditions with requirements for native plantings and pre-construction access review.

104-boston-road-water-appeal.name: 104 Boston Road water bill appeal
104-boston-road-water-appeal.description: Abatement appeal before the Water Commissioners regarding an underground leak and high water bill at 104 Boston Road.
104-boston-road-water-appeal.status: The appeal has been resolved. On September 15, the Select Board, acting as Water Commissioners, voted 4-0-1 to grant a partial abatement on the leak-related water bill, lowering the charge from $2,872.03 to $1,100. No further review or action is scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to grant a partial abatement, setting the final bill amount at $1,100.
A resident urged full bill relief for the property and called on the town to expedite smart water meter installations to prevent leak surprises.

12-darlene-drive-variance.name: 12 Darlene Drive setback variance
12-darlene-drive-variance.description: Front setback variance request to construct a covered front porch addition encroaching 1.5 feet into the setback at 12 Darlene Drive.
12-darlene-drive-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 4-0 on March 18, 2026, to approve a 1.5-foot front setback variance for a covered front porch addition at 12 Darlene Drive.

12-wood-street-special-permit.name: 12 Wood Street special permit
12-wood-street-special-permit.description: Special permit application to alter a pre-existing non-conforming single-family residential structure with a rear deck at 12 Wood Street.
12-wood-street-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved a special permit for 12 Wood Street on April 15, 2026, allowing a newly constructed deck sitting 13 feet from the rear boundary.

14-newton-street.name: 14 Newton Street garage and ADU
14-newton-street.description: Notice of Intent to construct a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit and replacement septic in the wetland buffer at 14 Newton Street.
14-newton-street.status: The proposed garage, accessory dwelling unit, and replacement septic system at 14 Newton Street have secured key local approvals. The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions in July 2026, and the Board of Health granted required setback variances in August 2026 despite concerns about expanding flow on a constrained lot. Before starting construction, the applicant must install erosion controls and obtain an inspection.

positions.detail: Voted 2-1 on Aug 11 to grant septic setback reductions from a town drain line, despite the chair dissenting against granting variance relief to expand system capacity on a constrained lot.
Voted 3-0-1 on Jul 29 to issue an Order of Conditions following plan adjustments to an infiltration drywell for roof runoff.

154-turnpike-road.name: 154 Turnpike Road site plan modification
154-turnpike-road.description: Major site plan approval modification and landscaping compliance for commercial development at 154 Turnpike Road.
154-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board is reviewing a major site plan modification for 154 Turnpike Road to address non-compliance regarding site lighting and landscaping. Capital Group Properties is installing dimmer switches and submitting revised sign lighting specifications to meet town standards, which board members plan to verify during an evening site visit. The public hearing is scheduled to resume on October 19, 2026, when the board expects to review a draft decision ahead of an extended October 23 statutory deadline.

positions.detail: Continued the hearing on September 28 to inspect lighting dimmer installations and prepare a draft decision for review on October 19, 2026.

154-turnpike-road.next: Continued public hearing and draft decision review before the Planning Board on October 19, 2026.

170-woodland-road-coc.name: 170 Woodland Road Certificate of Compliance
170-woodland-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for pool, patio, and drainage work within wetland resource areas at 170 Woodland Road.
170-woodland-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for completed residential work at 170 Woodland Road on June 4, 2026. The approval followed a site inspection confirming that required mitigation plantings and trees were healthy and in good condition. The review is complete, and no further action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on June 4, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after staff confirmed required mitigation plantings were healthy.

200-turnpike-road.name: 200 Turnpike Road site plan compliance
200-turnpike-road.description: Site plan compliance, occupancy permitting, and landscape performance bonding for a commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road.
200-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board accepted a $30,000 surety agreement and voted 5-0 to recommend that the building inspector issue a full certificate of occupancy for the commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road. The recommendation followed agreement on resolving winter landscaping die-off and slope erosion, backed by a performance bond through October 2027. A follow-up inspection is scheduled for fall 2027 to ensure plant survival and slope stability.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22 to accept a $30,000 surety agreement and recommend a full certificate of occupancy subject to landscaping conditions.

200-turnpike-road.next: Follow-up inspection for landscaping and slope stability by October 1, 2027

2030-master-plan-update.name: 2030 Master Plan update
2030-master-plan-update.description: Strategy, funding, and consultant selection for updating Southborough's comprehensive Master Plan for 2030.
2030-master-plan-update.status: The Master Plan Implementation Committee and Planning Board are coordinating on the process, timeline, and funding for Southborough's 2030 Master Plan update. MPIC recommends creating a new Master Plan Committee in 2027 and hiring a consultant under a hybrid model, with costs estimated between $40,000 and $100,000 funded through state grants or a Town Meeting warrant article. The Planning Board is reviewing the proposal but postponed formal adoption of its goals until the full board is present. The two boards will hold a joint discussion on October 19, 2026.

positions.detail: Recommends that the Planning Board lead the creation of a Master Plan Committee in 2027 using a hybrid volunteer-consultant model funded by grants or Town Meeting appropriation.
Reviewed the proposed 2027 timeline, hybrid approach, and funding options, but postponed formal goal adoption until all members are present.

2030-master-plan-update.next: Joint discussion between the Planning Board and Master Plan Implementation Committee on October 19, 2026.

21-coslin-drive-costco.name: 21 Coslin Drive Costco development
21-coslin-drive-costco.description: Site plan and special permit review for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco retail warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive.
21-coslin-drive-costco.status: The proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive is currently under major site plan and special permit review before the Planning Board. The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved height variances for retaining walls and parking lot light poles in July 2026, but the rest of the project remains under local and state review. Key unresolved concerns include regional traffic congestion on Route 9, truck turnaround impacts at Route 85, cut-through traffic on local roads, and Massachusetts Environmental Policy Act requirements. The Planning Board public hearing is scheduled to continue on October 19, 2026.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 15, 2026, to approve variances allowing retaining walls up to 31 feet and parking lot light poles up to 36.5 feet.
Currently evaluating Costco's major site plan and special permit applications while awaiting a consultant peer review on traffic.
Residents raised concerns regarding severe Route 9 traffic congestion, cut-through traffic on Flagg and Southville roads, truck damage to Route 85 guardrails, water pressure, and vehicle emissions.

21-coslin-drive-costco.next: Planning Board continued public hearing on October 19, 2026

21-highland-street-use.name: 21 Highland Street future use
21-highland-street-use.description: Planning for municipal department space allocation, community use, or potential sale of the town-owned building at 21 Highland Street.
21-highland-street-use.status: Space planning for 21 Highland Street remains under review as Youth and Family Services prepares to move to the Flagg School in late October. The Recreation Commission plans to absorb the vacated office space to expand after-school STEM and arts programming and create a civic meeting room. However, the long-term future of the municipal facility remains open following Select Board discussions regarding a potential sale of the property.

positions.detail: Supports repurposing space vacated by Youth and Family Services for after-school programming and town committee meeting rooms.

21-southville-road-coc.name: 21 Southville Road Certificate of Compliance
21-southville-road-coc.description: Request for a Certificate of Compliance under DEP file 290-1142 for a sunroom and patio within the wetland buffer zone at 21 Southville Road.
21-southville-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 on October 8 to issue a Certificate of Compliance for 21 Southville Road. The decision closes out the permit for converting a porch into a sunroom and patio within the wetland buffer zone. The conservation agent verified that the work is finished, the site's soils are stable, and a natural fence buffer was preserved.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 8 to approve the Certificate of Compliance after confirming the work is complete and the site is stable.

22-newton-street-variance.name: 22 Newton Street garage variance
22-newton-street-variance.description: Variance petition under Section 174-8.3(D)(3)(b) to construct a detached two-car garage encroaching on side lot line setbacks at 22 Newton Street.
22-newton-street-variance.status: The variance petition for 22 Newton Street has been withdrawn without prejudice. The Zoning Board of Appeals approved the withdrawal in June 2026 after board members raised concerns that the garage would sit on the side lot line and block access required for septic repairs. The homeowner is reconsidering design options, and no revised application has been filed.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10 to approve the applicant's withdrawal without prejudice following concerns regarding zero-foot setbacks and septic maintenance access.

22-turnpike-road.name: 22 Turnpike Road site plan modification
22-turnpike-road.description: Site plan modification to expand stormwater infiltration, permit existing patios and a shed, and address sports lighting at 22 Turnpike Road.
22-turnpike-road.status: The major site plan modification for the 22 Turnpike Road golf range is currently before the Planning Board while a draft decision is finalized following engineering peer review. The Conservation Commission previously cleared an equipment storage shed for the site under the Wetlands Protection Act in April 2026. The Planning Board is scheduled to review the draft decision at its continued public hearing on October 19, 2026, ahead of an October 23 decision deadline.

positions.detail: Continued the hearing without testimony on Sep 28 while a draft decision is prepared for review.
Voted 5-0 on Apr 30 to issue a negative determination of applicability with standard conditions for an equipment storage shed.

22-turnpike-road.next: Planning Board continued public hearing to review draft decision on October 19, 2026

229-parkerville-road-coc.name: 229 Parkerville Road Certificate of Compliance
229-parkerville-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and buffer zone encroachment resolution for a fenced garden at 229 Parkerville Road.
229-parkerville-road-coc.status: The Certificate of Compliance remains pending a final site inspection by the conservation agent scheduled for fall 2026. The Conservation Commission and the homeowner agreed on a resolution allowing an existing split-rail fence to stay in place as the permanent work limit while requiring garden trellises extending past the fence to be dismantled. Once staff confirms on-site that the encroaching trellises have been removed to allow natural revegetation, the certificate is expected to be issued.

positions.detail: Agreed on June 4 to allow the split-rail fence to remain, conditioning issuance of the certificate on the removal of encroaching garden trellises verified by a fall site visit.

229-parkerville-road-coc.next: Conservation agent site visit in fall 2026.

250-turnpike-road.name: 250 Turnpike Road 40B development
250-turnpike-road.description: Comprehensive permit application under Chapter 40B for residential development at 250 Turnpike Road.
250-turnpike-road.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit in May 2026 for a 32-unit rental townhouse development, but vertical construction cannot begin until wastewater and environmental permits are secured. The Conservation Commission's review of the project's Notice of Intent is ongoing and awaiting an environmental peer review report. Although the Board of Health granted a septic pump chamber variance in September 2026, the overall wastewater replacement plan still requires state and conservation approvals.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 6, 2026, to approve the comprehensive permit with revised conditions and waivers for the 32-unit project.
Continued the Notice of Intent hearing on Oct 8, 2026, while awaiting a peer review report from Lucas Environmental.
Voted 2-1 on Sep 15, 2026, to grant a foundation setback variance for the project's septic pump chamber subject to a vapor barrier condition.
Sent comments to the ZBA citing unaddressed concerns about property boundary shifts, tree discrepancies, and site plan noncompliance.
Abutters urged the town to downsize the project to 28 units, verify financial waivers, and mandate six-foot privacy fencing and stormwater protections near the Sudbury Reservoir watershed.

26-meadow-lane-coc.name: 26 Meadow Lane Certificate of Compliance
26-meadow-lane-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for trench drain installation and invasive species monitoring at 26 Meadow Lane under DEP File 290-1087.
26-meadow-lane-coc.status: The Conservation Commission voted unanimously on March 12, 2026, to issue a Certificate of Compliance for DEP File 290-1087 at 26 Meadow Lane following completed invasive species monitoring.

27-pine-hill-road-coc.name: 27 Pine Hill Road Certificate of Compliance
27-pine-hill-road-coc.description: Request for a Certificate of Compliance under DEP file 290-1128 for an inground pool within a riverfront area at 27 Pine Hill Road.
27-pine-hill-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for an in-ground pool at 27 Pine Hill Road on October 8, 2026. The conservation agent reported that all conditions were satisfied, including the installation of a split-rail fence, establishment of native shrubs, and overall site stability. With the certificate issued, the matter is concluded.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 8 to issue the Certificate of Compliance after the agent confirmed compliance with all conditions.

34-turnpike-road-special-permit.name: 34 Turnpike Road special permit
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.description: Special permit review and zoning compliance for unpermitted construction and renovations exceeding approvals at 34 Turnpike Road.
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted 1.3 feet of side setback relief to resolve as-built deviations on unpermitted construction, closing the public hearing on June 10, 2026. Approval is conditioned on the applicant removing an unauthorized foundation bump-out encroaching on septic setbacks and obtaining Board of Health certification that the septic capacity supports the dwelling's bedroom count. A formal review and determination from the Board of Health remain pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10, 2026, to approve the side setback relief on the condition that the Board of Health certifies septic capacity.
A representative for the abutter at 32 Turnpike Road opposed the relief, arguing the expansion created an unpermitted four-bedroom house with inadequate septic review.

355-turnpike-road-coc.name: 355 Turnpike Road Certificate of Compliance
355-turnpike-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review, unapproved paving, and stormwater maintenance for a commercial site at 355 Turnpike Road.
355-turnpike-road-coc.status: The request for a Certificate of Compliance for 355 Turnpike Road remains on hold before the Conservation Commission pending site cleanup and documentation. An August inspection revealed unpermitted pavement expansion, uncleaned catch basins showing an oil sheen, and an uncleared stormwater outlet. The commission kept the matter tabled without action on September 17 while awaiting basin maintenance and engineering clarification.

positions.detail: Tabled the Certificate of Compliance request pending catch basin maintenance, site cleanup, and engineering clarification on unpermitted paving.

40-42-central-street.name: 40-42 Central Street site plan compliance
40-42-central-street.description: Resolution of site plan discrepancies, parking configurations, and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street.
40-42-central-street.status: An appeal by the Southborough Historical Society challenging the building commissioner’s denial of a certificate of occupancy and a zoning violation for 40-42 Central Street is currently under review before the Zoning Board of Appeals. The Planning Board previously voted 4-1 to recommend revoking the property's temporary certificate of occupancy and met in executive session regarding threatened litigation from the owner. Key outstanding matters include paving and inspecting required accessible parking spaces, awaiting a written decision from the state Building Code Appeals Board, and resolving site plan approval issues. The ZBA's hearing is scheduled to resume on October 21, 2026.

positions.detail: Continued the appeal hearing to October 21, 2026, while accessible parking paving is completed and inspected and related compliance matters are resolved.
Voted 4-1 in May 2026 to recommend revoking the property's temporary certificate of occupancy and met in executive session over threatened litigation from the owner.
Appealed the building commissioner's denial of a certificate of occupancy and notice of zoning violation, and was granted continuances to finish paving accessible parking.

40-42-central-street.next: Zoning Board of Appeals continued hearing on October 21, 2026.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.name: 55-plus housing zoning bylaw amendment
55-plus-housing-bylaw.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment to eliminate caps on age-restricted 55-plus developments and clarify affordability requirements.
55-plus-housing-bylaw.status: The Affordable Housing Trust is drafting a zoning bylaw amendment that would eliminate the townwide cap on 55-plus housing units and establish a mandatory 12.5 percent affordability requirement. Trustees are also considering a two-acre minimum lot size with a base density of six units per acre via special permit to moderate neighborhood density impacts. A revised draft is scheduled for review at the trust's October 2026 meeting before being sent to Town Counsel and submitted to Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Drafting the proposed bylaw to eliminate senior housing caps and mandate 12.5 percent affordability, while exploring lot size standards to manage density.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.next: Presentation of the revised draft bylaw at the Affordable Housing Trust meeting in October 2026

6-lynbrook-road-enforcement-order.name: 6 Lynbrook Road enforcement order release
6-lynbrook-road-enforcement-order.description: Release of a 2013 Conservation Commission enforcement order regarding unpermitted work on adjacent DCR aqueduct land at 6 Lynbrook Road.
6-lynbrook-road-enforcement-order.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 on October 8 to lift a 2013 enforcement order against 6 Lynbrook Road. The outstanding order, uncovered during a title search for an ongoing home sale, concerned an unpermitted retaining wall and mowing on adjacent state aqueduct land. Following confirmation from the Department of Conservation and Recreation and a site inspection verifying the encroachments were removed, the matter is resolved and the deed cleared.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 8 to lift the enforcement order after verifying the retaining wall was removed and state land restored.

6-walker-street-variance.name: 6 Walker Street garage setback variance
6-walker-street-variance.description: Petition to modify a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance to construct a garage addition at 6 Walker Street.
6-walker-street-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved the application on July 15, 2026, modifying a 1965 variance condition to grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance for a garage addition at 6 Walker Street. Relief was granted based on site constraints and septic placement that made alternative locations impractical. The public hearing is closed, and no further board action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 15, 2026, to grant the variance relief citing practical difficulties with lot shape and septic location.
Abutters submitted letters of support for the variance, and no opposition was voiced.

65c-school-street-coc.name: 65C School Street Certificate of Compliance
65c-school-street-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review following unpermitted brush clearing and wetland buffer zone remediation at 65C School Street.
65c-school-street-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for 65C School Street on July 29, 2026. The approval followed remediation by the homeowner, who restored the 20-foot wetland buffer zone and submitted updated as-built plans after unpermitted brush clearing earlier in the year. The matter is resolved with no further town actions scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 29, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after confirming the buffer zone had been properly restored.

66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.name: 66 Breakneck Hill Road septic variance
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.description: Septic system upgrade and wetland setback variance to support converting a commercial building to residential use at 66 Breakneck Hill Road.
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved a septic variance on October 13 to support converting a commercial building at 66 Breakneck Hill Road into a four-bedroom single-family home. The variance allows an 85-foot wetland setback near drinking water tributaries instead of the standard 100 feet, improving upon the existing system's 79-foot setback. The project remains contingent on approval from the Conservation Commission and final sign-off from the health agent.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 13 to approve the variance, noting the upgraded nitrogen-reducing system improves upon existing conditions near the wetland.

7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.name: 7 Turnpike Road bodywork compliance
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.description: Town bodywork permitting compliance and cease-and-desist enforcement for an unlicensed massage business operating at 7 Turnpike Road.
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.status: The Board of Health unanimously denied the establishment license application for Jojo Bodywork following months of enforcement actions and operation during a cease-and-desist order. Health department staff and town counsel were authorized to draft and execute a formal written decision of the denial. No further hearings or proceedings are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 11 to deny the license application, citing missing practitioner credentials, unapproved aliases, and operation during an active cease-and-desist order.

8-partridge-hill-road-variance.name: 8 Partridge Hill Road septic variance
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.description: Septic repair variance regarding groundwater separation and setback to the Sudbury Reservoir at 8 Partridge Hill Road.
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved the requested variances on August 11, 2026, allowing the replacement of a failed 1975 septic system at 8 Partridge Hill Road. The approval permits a reduced groundwater separation of 2.5 feet and a setback of approximately 230 feet from the Sudbury Reservoir. The Department of Conservation and Recreation raised no objections to the direct-replacement plan, and no further municipal reviews are scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 11 to grant variances reducing groundwater separation to 2.5 feet and reservoir setback to approximately 230 feet.

911-field-bond-and-fees.name: 911 Field bond repayment and fees
911-field-bond-and-fees.description: Debt service repayment schedule and revolving fund athletic field user fees for the 911 Field turf complex.
911-field-bond-and-fees.status: The Recreation Commission is reviewing adjusted debt service schedules and a potential $5-per-hour field user fee increase to repay the remaining turf bond for the 911 Field complex. Annual revolving fund revenues have fallen short of initial projections, prompting discussions of extending $30,000 to $45,000 annual installments through FY35. The commission deferred formal action pending refined revenue models and fee proposals from the recreation and finance directors.

positions.detail: Weighing an extended debt payback plan and a modest fee increase for fall leagues, deferring a decision until updated financial projections are provided.

accessory-dwelling-units-zoning.name: Accessory Dwelling Units zoning amendment
accessory-dwelling-units-zoning.description: Zoning bylaw amendments aligning local regulations with state Affordable Homes Act requirements for accessory dwelling units.
accessory-dwelling-units-zoning.status: The Advisory Committee voted 2-5 to recommend disapproval of Article 29, which would allow ADUs up to 1,200 square feet by right, sending the article to the April 11, 2026 Annual Town Meeting floor.

affordable-housing-trust-zoning-cleanup.name: Affordable Housing Trust code reference cleanup
affordable-housing-trust-zoning-cleanup.description: Town Meeting warrant article updating the zoning code to replace references to SHOPC with the Southborough Affordable Housing Trust.
affordable-housing-trust-zoning-cleanup.status: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend approval of Article 30 to update zoning references to the Affordable Housing Trust, and the Planning Board continued its public hearing on the article to April 11, 2026.

algonquin-cell-phone-policy.name: Algonquin high school cell phone policy
algonquin-cell-phone-policy.description: Cell phone restrictions and evaluation of geofencing software at Algonquin Regional High School.
algonquin-cell-phone-policy.status: Algonquin Regional High School's planned rollout of the Doorman geofencing mobile app is on indefinite hold following technical delays and community concerns over student surveillance and data privacy. Classrooms are continuing to use in-room canvas caddies to restrict phone access while long-term options are evaluated. School administration plans to gather further input from students and the community through a steering committee before moving forward.

positions.detail: Residents and a student opposed the Doorman app, citing student privacy, data security risks, and questions over whether policy authority rests with the school committee rather than staff.

appointed-town-clerk.name: Appointed town clerk transition
appointed-town-clerk.description: Proposal to transition the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position, including interim clerk appointments.
appointed-town-clerk.status: Article 1, which proposes transitioning the Town Clerk from an elected office to a Select Board-appointed position with a term of up to three years, goes before Special Town Meeting on October 17, 2026. Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee unanimously recommend approval to widen the candidate pool for an increasingly technical role, though Advisory noted concerns about losing direct voter control and recommended contractual termination-for-cause protections. If passed by Town Meeting, the transition would still require ratification through a ballot question at the May 11, 2027 town election or a special act of the legislature. In the interim, appointed clerk Amy Berry is serving through May 11, 2027 following Jim Hegarty's retirement.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 1 to change the position from elected to appointed.
Voted 6-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval, citing a broader applicant pool for technical work while advising termination-for-cause safeguards.

appointed-town-clerk.next: Special Town Meeting vote on Article 1 on October 17, 2026.

atwood-property-remediation.name: Atwood property environmental remediation
atwood-property-remediation.description: Capital borrowing and environmental site remediation planning for the municipal Atwood property.
atwood-property-remediation.status: Town officials canceled current contract bids and removed the $820,000 Atwood site soil remediation request from the Annual Town Meeting warrant, planning to re-bid and present Article 9 at the fall special town meeting.

board-of-health-body-art-regulations.name: Board of Health body art regulations
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.description: Revisions to municipal body art regulations regarding practitioner training, apprenticeships, and prohibited activities.
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved updated local body art regulations in June 2026. The revised rules align with state model language by setting standards for apprenticeships, requiring practitioner training in CPR, first aid, anatomy, and bloodborne pathogens, and prohibiting vaping in procedure areas. With the vote concluded, the regulations are now established as local enforceable rules.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on June 9 to approve the revised regulations, including an amendment adding vaping to prohibited activities in procedure areas.

breakneck-hill-restoration.name: Breakneck Hill Conservation Land restoration
breakneck-hill-restoration.description: Planning and invasive species management for a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration at Breakneck Hill Conservation Land.
breakneck-hill-restoration.status: The Stewardship Committee is preparing a formal scope of work with the town planner to solicit bids for a five-zone ecological restoration of Breakneck Hill Conservation Land. The project addresses invasive species management, soil compaction from heavy equipment, site grading, botanical surveys, and native replanting, utilizing $47,000 recovered from remediation contractors. A committee liaison was appointed in August to coordinate with the invasive management contractor as planning proceeds.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to appoint a liaison to the invasive plant management contractor while developing a comprehensive restoration scope with the town planner.

brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.name: Brox asphalt plant complaints
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.description: Intermunicipal response and MassDEP oversight regarding resident noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough.
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.status: Southborough continues to monitor noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough, though Town Counsel has advised that the town lacks regulatory jurisdiction over the out-of-town facility. While MassDEP found the plant meets emissions standards and Brox recently installed an exhaust mitigation system, nearby residents continue to report odors. Health officials are advising residents to submit detailed real-time logs directly to MassDEP to help regulators identify operational patterns.

positions.detail: Monitoring resident reports and coordinating with MassDEP while acknowledging the town lacks legal enforcement authority over the Marlborough plant.
Residents reported persistent chemical odors and early-morning noise, with one neighbor urging both towns to fund an independent air quality study.

cannabis-delivery-opt-out.name: Cannabis delivery opt-out waiver
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.description: Deliberation on whether Southborough should request a state waiver from the Cannabis Control Commission to prohibit adult-use cannabis home delivery.
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.status: Adult-use cannabis home delivery is permitted in Southborough after the Select Board voted against applying for a state opt-out waiver. The Board of Health reviewed the issue earlier without taking a formal stance, weighing youth access concerns against parity with alcohol delivery. With the opt-out rejected, licensed couriers may deliver to adult residents aged 21 and older, and no further action is scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 1-4 on Aug 11 against applying for a two-year state opt-out waiver, allowing licensed home delivery to proceed.
Declined to take a formal stance on July 7, sending the Select Board a memo outlining divided views on youth health risks versus adult access.
A resident favored opting out, questioning whether doorstep ID checks would be enforced and doubting any public benefit.

cemetery-expansion.name: Town cemetery expansion planning
cemetery-expansion.description: Site evaluation and capacity planning to identify and acquire land for a new municipal cemetery.
cemetery-expansion.status: Town cemetery expansion planning is under review as the ad hoc Cemetery Expansion Committee evaluates 58 candidate parcels of five or more acres for a new municipal cemetery. With Rural Cemetery sold out and Middle Road Cemetery projected to reach capacity around 2035 or 2036, the committee is developing a screening matrix to narrow down potential sites. The Select Board backs the planning effort and voted in September to reduce the committee's size to maintain quorums. The committee expects to present final site recommendations before June.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to reduce the expansion committee's membership to three to achieve quorums and maintain progress on capacity planning.
Is vetting 58 candidate properties of five or more acres to recommend a site before Middle Road Cemetery exhausts its remaining 458 plots.

classification-and-compensation-study.name: Municipal classification and compensation study
classification-and-compensation-study.description: A comprehensive classification and compensation study evaluating 48 non-union municipal employee positions.
classification-and-compensation-study.status: A comprehensive classification and compensation study evaluating 48 non-union municipal positions is under review, with consultant MGT finalizing data collection from peer communities. The Personnel Board has placed individual job reclassification requests on hold to evaluate all positions collectively once findings are delivered. Final recommendations are expected to come before the Annual Town Meeting in March 2027.

positions.detail: Overseeing the study and voted 3-1 in July to approve the peer communities list excluding Dover, while holding individual reclassifications until final results are delivered.
Voted 5-0 on March 10 to support the warrant article authorizing the compensation study.
A municipal employee expressed concern in August over removing Dover from the comparable communities list, urging adherence to the consultant's independent process.

classification-and-compensation-study.next: Presentation of study recommendations at Annual Town Meeting, March 2027

classroom-interactive-touch-displays.name: Classroom interactive touch displays
classroom-interactive-touch-displays.description: A $365,000 capital request for the Annual Town Meeting warrant to install Newline interactive touch displays across K-8 classrooms.
classroom-interactive-touch-displays.status: The School Committee is requesting $365,000 at the April 11, 2026 Annual Town Meeting to replace obsolete classroom projectors across K-8 schools with Newline interactive touch displays.

community-preservation-appropriations.name: Community Preservation statutory appropriations
community-preservation-appropriations.description: Annual Town Meeting appropriations for Community Preservation Act statutory reserves, debt service, and administrative expenses.
community-preservation-appropriations.status: The Select Board voted 4-0-1 in March 2026 to support Article 22, which provides annual Community Preservation Act statutory reserve allocations and $29,000 in administrative expenses. During that review, board members pressed on why 18 older CPA projects remained open, which Community Preservation Committee leadership explained was due to pending statutory signage installation. With the 2026 Annual Town Meeting cycle concluded, the Community Preservation Committee has turned to preliminary technical reviews of draft applications for the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on March 10, 2026, to support Article 22, while urging the consolidation and standardization of signage to close out legacy projects faster.
Sponsored Article 22 to establish statutory reserves and fund administrative expenses, noting that legacy projects remain open primarily to satisfy signage requirements.

conservation-land-use-regulations.name: Conservation land use regulations
conservation-land-use-regulations.description: Adoption and amendment of town code regulations governing public use and activities on town-owned conservation land.
conservation-land-use-regulations.status: The Conservation Commission adopted regulations governing town-owned conservation land under Section 43-2 of the Southborough Town Code in April 2026. The regulations incorporated feedback from the Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee and were filed with the town clerk. The commission noted that future amendments may be considered to address issues such as light trespass from abutting parcels.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on April 30, 2026, to formally adopt the land use regulations under Town Code Section 43-2.

constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.name: Constitution Drive drainage and street acceptance
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.description: Sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive and resolution of unrecorded municipal street and drainage easements.
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.status: The Select Board authorized DPW to perform an estimated $5,000 one-time sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive, conditioned on a signed right-of-entry and hold-harmless agreement from the homeowner. The recurring sinkhole sits over a 17.5-foot-deep town storm drainage pipe on a street where Town Meeting approved acceptance in the past, but final deeds were never recorded. Town staff and town counsel are currently investigating options to resolve the unrecorded street and drainage easements.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2 to authorize DPW's driveway repair under a hold-harmless agreement and directed staff to explore legal steps to rectify unrecorded easements.

costco-special-act-liquor-license.name: Costco special act liquor license
costco-special-act-liquor-license.description: Proposed special state legislation authorizing an additional off-premises liquor license in Southborough for Costco.
costco-special-act-liquor-license.status: Special state legislation authorizing Southborough to issue an additional off-premises all-alcohol license for Costco is pending at the State House. Under refined draft language, the town would have two years to grant the license, which would revert to the state if left unused for three years. The Select Board unanimously supports the measure and agreed to submit testimony in favor of the bill.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 to back the home rule petition in March and agreed in June to submit written testimony supporting the special legislation.

cpa-project-signage-program.name: CPA project signage program
cpa-project-signage-program.description: Development of townwide signage and markers for past and ongoing Community Preservation Act-funded projects.
cpa-project-signage-program.status: The Community Preservation Committee is actively carrying out a townwide program to place bronze plaques and PVC signs at past and ongoing CPA-funded sites, funded by leftover balances in individual project accounts. The committee has finalized text and placements for several locations, including the Town House, Fay Park, and Mooney Field, and has coordinated with partner boards such as the Library Trustees. Work remains ongoing to finalize sign proofs and mounting locations across remaining sites before placing orders.

positions.detail: Leading the rollout of permanent bronze and PVC signs across more than 20 CPA project sites using remaining account balances.
Agreed to install exterior and interior plaques recognizing CPA funding for the facade restoration and historical collection archiving.
A resident suggested standardizing markers with a QR code and webpage link to cut costs, prevent sign clutter, and allow updates.

culvert-infrastructure-replacements.name: Culvert infrastructure replacements
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.description: Town-wide culvert replacements funded through a state grant to replace previously authorized borrowing.
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.status: Town-wide culvert infrastructure work is moving forward after the Select Board unanimously accepted three permanent drainage easements along Willow Street in August 2026 to support ongoing replacements and state permitting. The work is funded by a nearly $3.9 million award from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program announced in June 2026, which allows the town to complete the projects without using debt. The $3.9 million in borrowing previously authorized at Town Meeting can now eventually be rescinded.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on August 11, 2026, to accept the three Willow Street drainage easements needed to advance the grant-funded culvert work.
Voted 6-0 on March 25, 2026, to recommend approval of the Town Meeting warrant article authorizing the Willow Street easements.

decertified-library-borrowing-policy.name: Decertified library borrowing policy
decertified-library-borrowing-policy.description: Library Board of Trustees policy restricting physical borrowing privileges for patrons from municipalities with decertified public libraries.
decertified-library-borrowing-policy.status: The Library Board of Trustees approved a policy restricting physical borrowing privileges for patrons residing in municipalities with decertified public libraries. Under the policy, affected patrons retain building access, computer access, and event attendance, while CW MARS will block physical item checkouts. Trustees noted the policy can be revisited if neighboring towns face decertification in future budget cycles.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Oct 5 to adopt the CW MARS model policy restricting physical borrowing for patrons from decertified communities.

downtown-wayfinding-plan.name: Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan
downtown-wayfinding-plan.description: A state grant-funded planning study to design and install directional, gateway, and informational signage across downtown Southborough.
downtown-wayfinding-plan.status: The draft wayfinding plan to install gateway, directional, and pedestrian signage across downtown Southborough remains under review by town officials. While reviewing early concepts, the Select Board and Historical Commission cautioned against visual clutter and suburban aesthetics, urging consultants to incorporate omitted historic destinations such as the Community House, Rural Cemetery, and Burnett Mansion. Town administration plans to seek a Phase 2 state grant to fund detailed fabrication specifications and eventual sign installation.

positions.detail: Cautions against sign clutter and modern suburban designs, while insisting that key historic landmarks must be integrated into the wayfinding system.
Reviewed the draft plan in June 2026, noting community preference for simpler designs and requesting the addition of historic locations before pursuing fabrication grants.

facilities-van-replacement.name: Facilities Department replacement van
facilities-van-replacement.description: Emergency capital funding and potential Reserve Fund transfer to replace an out-of-service Facilities Department van.
facilities-van-replacement.status: The Advisory Committee voted 5-0 on March 16, 2026, to approve an emergency $75,000 Reserve Fund transfer to replace the Facilities Department utility van, removing the item from the capital warrant article.

fay-school-25-middle-road.name: Fay School 25 Middle Road addition
fay-school-25-middle-road.description: Review of as-built plans, construction discrepancies, and landscape mitigation for an addition at Fay School's 25 Middle Road campus.
fay-school-25-middle-road.status: Fay School is seeking a final certificate of occupancy for its 25 Middle Road addition following the Planning Board's August approval of a temporary certificate. The board is reviewing an updated landscape mitigation plan to resolve construction discrepancies involving tree removals and non-native plantings, while peer review of as-built engineering plans remains pending. Key points under review include ensuring plants are free of neonicotinoid pesticides, finalizing enforceable conditions, and addressing invasive species. The Planning Board will resume its review on October 19, 2026.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on August 17 to recommend a temporary certificate of occupancy and is reviewing landscape mitigation and peer-reviewed as-built drawings before approving final compliance.
A resident involved with biodiversity efforts urged that mitigation plantings be certified free of neonicotinoid pesticides, exclude non-native cultivars, and eradicate invasive species.

fay-school-athletic-fields.name: Fay School athletic fields redevelopment
fay-school-athletic-fields.description: Notice of Intent and redevelopment to convert grass soccer fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlboro Junction property.
fay-school-athletic-fields.status: The Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit application to convert grass fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlborough Junction property remains under review. The Conservation Commission has not yet deliberated on the merits of work within the wetland buffer zone and riverfront area, having granted repeated continuance requests from the applicant without substantive presentation. A substantive public hearing before the commission will be the next step once rescheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Oct 8 to continue the public hearing at the applicant's request without substantive discussion.

fayville-memorial-park-improvements.name: Fayville Memorial Park improvements
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.description: Planning, community outreach, and design improvements for Fayville Memorial Park, including splash pad features and parking capacity.
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.status: The Recreation Commission has postponed its roughly $1.5 million Community Preservation Act application for park renovations to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting while parking designs are resolved. The commission favors adding angled street parking along Central Street to avoid encroaching on the park's green space, but the Select Board has requested further engineering details regarding sight lines and vehicle buffers before taking a position. In the meantime, officials are examining potential Article 97 open space restrictions, testing interim parallel parking striping, and awaiting the outcome of a federal grant that could cover half of eligible costs.

positions.detail: Champions the renovation project and prefers angled street parking along Central Street over paving parkland, opting to defer its funding request to spring 2027 to resolve design and open space questions.
Reviewed the angled street parking concept on September 2 and requested additional engineering and design details regarding traffic safety and sight lines.
A resident opposed angled street parking due to traffic speeds and sight line concerns, while other comments addressed ADA accessibility and operating rules for a proposed dog park.

flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.name: Flagg Road and Route 9 hydrant relocation
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.description: Relocation of a frequently struck fire hydrant and removal of scenic road stone wall at Flagg Road and 361 Turnpike Road.
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.status: The project is approved to move forward after the Planning Board granted permission to dismantle approximately 10 feet of scenic road stone wall. The removal allows the Department of Public Works to relocate a frequently struck fire hydrant roughly 10 feet back into a newly acquired utility easement. Approval was granted with conditions requiring the removed stones to remain on Flagg Road or be reused in adjacent wall restoration.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to approve the stone wall removal on the condition that removed stones remain on Flagg Road or be reused for wall reconstruction.

fy27-operating-budget.name: FY27 operating budget
fy27-operating-budget.description: Annual municipal operating budget, revenue cap balancing, and omnibus warrant article for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-operating-budget.status: The Advisory Committee finalized its Annual Town Meeting booklet report on the omnibus budget and multi-year deficits, while town boards coordinated floor presentations for the April 11, 2026 Town Meeting.

fy27-road-paving-contracts.name: FY27 road paving and sidewalk contracts
fy27-road-paving-contracts.description: Procurement and contract awards for fiscal year 2027 DPW road paving and sidewalk maintenance.
fy27-road-paving-contracts.status: The Select Board unanimously approved the fiscal year 2027 contracts for road paving and sidewalk maintenance on September 15, 2026. The awarded contract covers six roads, including interim paving on Cordaville and Cranberry roads ahead of long-term state Transportation Improvement Program projects. Bid pricing came in approximately $400,000 below engineering estimates, and no further municipal approvals are required.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to approve the FY27 paving and sidewalk contract awards, noting bids came in well below estimates.

fy27-school-operating-budget.name: FY27 school operating budget
fy27-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, class size staffing, and reserve funding for the Southborough K-8 public schools for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-school-operating-budget.status: The FY27 school operating budget is in execution, showing an available first-quarter balance of $349,347 (1.34 percent) after absorbing two additional elementary teachers hired to maintain class sizes. On October 14, the School Committee approved internal line-item transfers to resolve deficits in curriculum salaries, fuel, water, and special education transportation without requiring new funding. The committee also requested that the Select Board deposit $105,485 in unexpected state Chapter 70 aid into the currently empty Special Education Stabilization Fund to buffer against future out-of-district placement costs.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 14 to approve first-quarter budget line-item transfers and requested the Select Board direct $105,485 in additional state aid to special education reserves.

fy27-water-enterprise-budget.name: FY27 Water Enterprise budget and capital
fy27-water-enterprise-budget.description: Annual operating budget, non-borrowing capital improvements, and loan authorizations for the Water Enterprise Fund.
fy27-water-enterprise-budget.status: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee voted 3-0 to support Article 10 for water fund capital items on the Annual Town Meeting warrant, joining prior Select Board support.

fy28-operating-budget.name: FY28 operating budget
fy28-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, multi-year deficit forecasting, and consideration of a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-operating-budget.status: Facing a projected $2 million deficit in FY28 that could require a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override, town officials directed departments to submit dual budget requests: a level-service plan with 5% salary increases and a zero-growth plan requiring staffing and operational cuts. Several boards have approved their level-service requests, but others face reductions to staff hours under the no-growth scenario. The Select Board and Advisory Committee remain in early planning over whether to seek an override—and whether it should span a single year or multiple years—or enforce tighter spending limits. The two boards will begin reviewing departmental submissions jointly on November 4, 2026.

positions.detail: Exploring whether to ask voters for an operational override—potentially covering up to five years—to address a projected $2 million deficit, while requiring departments to model zero-growth cut scenarios.
Urged caution regarding a large multi-year override, suggesting the town consider alternatives such as a hiring freeze, position backfill reviews, or borrowing mechanisms for unfunded pensions.
Voted 4-0 on September 8 to recommend a 5% total salary adjustment for FY28, combining a 3% cost-of-living adjustment with 2% step increases.
Voted 5-0 on October 14 to approve its FY28 budget priorities to guide the administration's preliminary budget build.
Voted 6-0 on October 5 to approve its FY28 operating budget, warning that an override failure would eliminate programming and reduce database subscriptions by over half.
Voted unanimously on October 7 to approve a $4,250 operating budget request after resolving trail mowing contract allocations.
Approved its small elected board budget but deferred its department operating budget vote to a special meeting after an agenda posting omission.
Postponed a vote on its FY28 request while expressing strong frustration that town guidance for zero-growth budgets would require cutting the conservation agent's hours.

Residents suggested consolidating departmental budgets to improve efficiency, cautioned that departing from traditional line-item formats could raise voter skepticism, and noted that Town Meeting can vote on contingent budgets.

fy28-operating-budget.next: Board of Health special meeting to review and approve its FY28 operating budget on October 20, 2026.

fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.name: FY28 regional school operating budget
fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, health insurance restructuring, and capital improvement planning for the Northborough-Southborough Regional School District for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.status: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School District is developing its FY28 operating budget amid tight municipal revenue constraints under Proposition 2 1/2. District subcommittees are pursuing several cost-containment measures, including restructuring employee healthcare deductibles to save an estimated $600,000 and proposing Special Education Stabilization Funds at both town meetings. To accommodate differing guidance from Southborough and Northborough, administrators are modeling level-service, 3% capped, and level-funded scenarios. Initial departmental budget requests are due October 20, 2026, ahead of preliminary presentations to the full Regional School Committee.

positions.body: Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee Operational Budget and Capital Planning Subcommittees
positions.detail: Reviewed five draft strategic priorities on Oct 7 and directed administrators to prepare multiple budget tiers to align with municipal fiscal constraints.
A speaker suggested holding earlier joint discussions so municipal financial committees and the school district share budget assumptions and terminology.

fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.next: School administrators submit FY28 budget requests to district finance on October 20, 2026.

glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.name: Glow SoBo holiday lighting
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.description: Funding and municipal installation of holiday lighting displays and kickoff event for the Tricentennial.
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.status: Plans for the Glow SoBo holiday lighting display and celebration are moving forward for early December. The Tricentennial Committee authorized a $10,456 contract for commercial exterior lighting of the Town House, library grounds, and nearby trees, and will fund permanent exterior electrical outlets on the library property. The Library Board of Trustees unanimously approved the outdoor lighting and electrical work, while deferring any decision on hosting indoor after-hours activities.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Aug 12 to approve a $10,456 contract for professional lighting on municipal buildings and grounds.
Voted unanimously on Sep 14 to approve exterior holiday lighting and the installation of permanent outdoor electrical outlets.

hopkinton-water-connection.name: Hopkinton MWRA water connection
hopkinton-water-connection.description: Proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to the town of Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution system.
hopkinton-water-connection.status: A proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution network is currently under negotiation after talks resumed following a stall in 2023. Under the framework being discussed, Hopkinton would cover pumping and maintenance costs, fund curb-to-curb roadway repaving where mains are installed, and pay $1 million toward local water projects, while engineering plans include replacing the Oak Hill Road water tank subject to Zoning Board of Appeals approval. The project still requires state approvals for Hopkinton and an independent engineering peer review for Southborough. The Select Board has not taken a position on the agreement and plans to vote at an upcoming meeting to appoint special municipal counsel to negotiate contract terms due to a conflict of interest with town counsel.

housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.name: Housing and food health code enforcement policies
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.description: Board of Health standardized enforcement procedures, violation correction timelines, and fee schedules for housing and food establishments.
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.status: Proposed enforcement policies and fee schedules for housing and food health code violations remain under review by the Board of Health. The board tabled formal approval in August to allow staff to clarify how written correction deadlines are determined based on violation severity. A revised draft is pending further review and formal adoption.

positions.detail: Favors standardizing stepped fees and enforcement for repeat violations, but tabled approval to ensure correction timelines clearly reflect violation severity.

independent-finance-committee-bylaw.name: Independent finance committee citizen petition
independent-finance-committee-bylaw.description: Citizen petition warrant article proposing to establish an independent finance committee to oversee town accounting and purchasing.
independent-finance-committee-bylaw.status: The Advisory Committee reviewed Jack Baron's citizen petition for Article 33 proposing an independent finance committee, taking no formal vote and deferring action directly to the Annual Town Meeting floor.

industrial-park-zoning-amendments.name: Industrial Park zoning amendments
industrial-park-zoning-amendments.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendments establishing local definitions and regulations for battery energy storage systems and data centers in the Industrial Park district.
industrial-park-zoning-amendments.status: The Planning Board opened a public hearing on March 30, 2026, regarding Section 174-9 to designate itself as the special permit granting authority for data centers under Article 17. The hearing was continued to April 11, 2026, immediately prior to Annual Town Meeting.

kallander-field-repairs.name: Kallander Field turf repairs
kallander-field-repairs.description: Scoping, vendor pricing, and DPW coordination for repairing turf and playing surface conditions at Kallander Field.
kallander-field-repairs.status: Repair plans for Kallander Field remain under review by the Recreation Commission. The original turf installer proposed completing the work for $8,000 to $9,000 with Department of Public Works assistance, well below earlier $40,000 estimates and within the commission's available capital funds. The commission discussed the proposal in May 2026 but had not yet taken formal action.

positions.detail: Reviewed an $8,000 to $9,000 repair estimate from the original turf installer in May 2026 but deferred formal action.

kratom-retail-ban.name: Statewide kratom ban and local enforcement
kratom-retail-ban.description: Local Board of Health enforcement and retail monitoring following the state's Schedule I temporary ban on kratom.
kratom-retail-ban.status: Southborough health staff have reviewed local stores following the state's one-year temporary Schedule I classification of kratom, which took effect in August 2026. Only one Southborough retailer was found carrying kratom products, and staff provided guidance on securing, returning, or lawfully disposing of remaining inventory. The Board of Health received the update in September 2026, with no further local board action required.

landfill-environmental-assessment.name: Southborough landfill environmental assessment
landfill-environmental-assessment.description: Environmental risk assessment, private well testing, and potential municipal water line extension regarding contamination from the Southborough landfill.
landfill-environmental-assessment.status: Article 7 on the Special Town Meeting warrant requests $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend a water main and connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill. The extension is intended to eliminate private well contamination risks and avoid state-mandated PFAS testing. Both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee recommend approval after clarifying that the town will cover the service lines from the street into the houses. The appropriation now awaits a vote at Special Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Oct 6 to recommend Article 7 after confirming the town will pay for the connection lines from the street to the houses.
Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to recommend Article 7 to eliminate well contamination risks and avoid ongoing state testing mandates.

latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.name: Latisquama Road errant golf balls
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.description: Safety concerns and mitigation options regarding errant golf balls striking residential properties on Latisquama Road from the Southborough Golf Club.
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.status: The Golf Committee is evaluating mitigation options to address errant golf balls from the Southborough Golf Club striking homes on Latisquama Road. Members are considering whether to move the 7th tee box, reorient the green, or convert the hole into a par 3 after prior netting and relocations failed to resolve property damage. The committee intends to consult the course architect on hole redesign options as a standing agenda item.

positions.detail: Seeking recommendations from the golf architect on redesigning the 7th hole following neighborhood reports of significant property damage.

library-book-drop-repair.name: Library book drop concrete repair
library-book-drop-repair.description: Repair and funding of damaged concrete beneath the Southborough Library book drop and clarification of municipal maintenance responsibilities.
library-book-drop-repair.status: The Library Board of Trustees approved replacing the damaged concrete pad beneath the book drop for under $5,000 using library State Aid funds. In response to recurring disputes over whether the Department of Public Works or the library oversees exterior property upkeep, the trustees also voted to send a letter to town officials to clarify maintenance responsibilities. Work was scheduled for early October 2026.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 11, 2026 to fund the pad replacement using State Aid and to draft a letter clarifying DPW and library maintenance duties.

library-cpa-signage.name: Library CPA commemorative signage
library-cpa-signage.description: Design and wording of commemorative plaques crediting Community Preservation Act funding for Southborough Library restoration projects.
library-cpa-signage.status: The Community Preservation Committee and the Library Board of Trustees have agreed on the design and text for commemorative plaques recognizing past Community Preservation Act funding for the library's facade restoration and local history collection. The bronze plaques will feature the town seal and thank Southborough 'residents' rather than 'taxpayers' or 'citizens.' The signs have been commissioned, and invoices have been submitted to the CPC for reimbursement to formally close out the grants.

positions.detail: Supported plaque language thanking 'residents' and reported in August that signs have been commissioned and invoices sent to the CPC.
Voted 5-1 on July 21 to approve plaques crediting Southborough residents and displaying the town seal, over one member's preference for 'taxpayers' to reflect business contributions.

library-hotspot-lending-policy.name: Library wireless hotspot lending policy
library-hotspot-lending-policy.description: Policy revisions and fee structures for circulating mobile Wi-Fi hotspots borrowed from the Southborough Library.
library-hotspot-lending-policy.status: The Library Board of Trustees unanimously approved the revised circulating wireless hotspot lending policy on September 14, 2026. The updated rules mandate direct in-person returns to staff, establish a $15 replacement fee for lost or unreturned chargers directed to the town general fund, and allow six-month borrowing suspensions for repeat violations. No further board approvals or hearings are required.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 14 to adopt the revised hotspot lending rules, charger replacement fees, and suspension terms.

library-parking-lot-repaving.name: Library parking lot repaving
library-parking-lot-repaving.description: Capital planning, DPW coordination, and town warrant sponsorship for repaving the Southborough Library parking lot.
library-parking-lot-repaving.status: Repaving of the Southborough Library parking lot has been deferred and will not be submitted as a capital request for FY28. Site engineering requirements to manage runoff and protect the water table added granite features that drove up costs beyond what could be funded near-term or covered by library state aid. The project is instead slated to be proposed for town capital planning in two to three years.

positions.detail: Agreed to defer the capital repaving request for two to three years due to elevated engineering costs for drainage and water table protection.

lynbrook-road-water-main-rehabilitation.name: Lynbrook Road water main rehabilitation
lynbrook-road-water-main-rehabilitation.description: Notice of Intent and cured-in-place structural lining of an aging 12-inch water main along I-495 and Lynbrook Road.
lynbrook-road-water-main-rehabilitation.status: The Conservation Commission unanimously approved an Order of Conditions on April 2, 2026, for the DPW's Lynbrook Road water main replacement project. Work remains subject to pre-construction submittals and dewatering reviews.

masc-calendar-study-resolution.name: MASC statewide school calendar study resolution
masc-calendar-study-resolution.description: Resolution sponsored through the Massachusetts Association of School Committees seeking a state study on school calendar configurations.
masc-calendar-study-resolution.status: The combined Northborough, Southborough, and Regional school committees deferred action on a joint MASC resolution requesting a statewide study of school calendars, scheduling individual committee votes for April 2026 ahead of the June 1 submission deadline.

mbta-communities-zoning-correction.name: MBTA Communities zoning table correction
mbta-communities-zoning-correction.description: Town Meeting warrant article to correct transcription errors in the MBTA Communities Overlay District dimensional table.
mbta-communities-zoning-correction.status: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend approval of Article 31, while the Planning Board continued its public hearing on the dimensional table correction to April 11, 2026, ahead of Annual Town Meeting.

mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.name: McAuliffe Hearing Room audiovisual upgrades
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.description: Hardware, camera framing, and video conferencing upgrades for hybrid public meetings in the McAuliffe Hearing Room at the Town House.
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.status: Audiovisual upgrades in the McAuliffe Hearing Room have been installed and are undergoing configuration and fine-tuning. Adjustments have addressed dais monitor visibility and microphone tuning, though displaying remote attendees to in-person audiences remains an open issue. The Municipal Technology Committee is continuing to track user feedback as technicians resolve remaining software and framing settings.

positions.detail: Supports the hybrid meeting upgrades and continues to monitor user feedback while technicians resolve remaining display and software configurations.

metrowest-recc-borrowing.name: MetroWest RECC borrowing authorization
metrowest-recc-borrowing.description: Short-term borrowing authorization of up to $12.5 million to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
metrowest-recc-borrowing.status: The Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing authority in May 2026 to serve as bridge financing between state 911 grant disbursements for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center. The authorization aligned Southborough with partner towns Grafton and Westborough, despite debate over taking on regional borrowing risk. Outstanding resident concerns focus on municipal exposure to ongoing lease, legal, and insurance expenses.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on May 19 to approve up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing notes to keep construction on schedule, over one member's objection to assuming regional debt risk.
A resident raised concerns regarding town liability for leasehold improvements, legal fees, and insurance costs under the regional lease agreement.

multi-year-road-and-sidewalk-borrowing.name: Multi-year road and sidewalk borrowing
multi-year-road-and-sidewalk-borrowing.description: Proposed multi-million dollar capital borrowing authorization and debt exclusion for comprehensive road and sidewalk improvements.
multi-year-road-and-sidewalk-borrowing.status: The Select Board revoted 4-0-1 to recommend approval of Article 13 for $25 million in road and sidewalk borrowing at Annual Town Meeting, and voted 5-0 to place the debt exclusion on the May 12, 2026 town election ballot.

municipal-financial-policies.name: Municipal financial policies adoption
municipal-financial-policies.description: Review and formal adoption of town financial policies recommended by the Massachusetts Division of Local Services.
municipal-financial-policies.status: The Select Board has adopted six municipal financial policies—including purchasing, investments, and anti-fraud controls—while shelving state-recommended reserve targets because the town does not currently meet those levels. Draft policies covering procurement confidentiality, grant management, senior tax work-offs, and budget development remain under review. Key open questions involve clarifying RFP pricing procedures under state procurement law and defining the statutory roles of the Select Board, Town Administrator, and Advisory Committee in the budget process. No further hearing or vote is currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Has approved six administrative policies but shelved state reserve recommendations and postponed votes on budget, procurement, and grant rules pending legal and committee review.
Residents suggested establishing a centralized database to track grant lifecycles and proposed eliminating income limits on the senior tax work-off program.

municipal-grants-management-policy.name: Municipal Grants Management Policy
municipal-grants-management-policy.description: Town oversight and approval procedures governing municipal grant applications, match funding, and operational liabilities.
municipal-grants-management-policy.status: The Municipal Grants Management Policy was adopted following unanimous approval by the Select Board in April 2026. The policy sets municipal oversight and approval procedures for grant applications, local match funding, and ongoing operational liabilities. No further board reviews or updates are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 28, 2026, to approve the Grants Management Financial Policy as amended.

municipal-health-insurance-reform.name: Municipal employee health insurance reform
municipal-health-insurance-reform.description: Adoption of MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21-23 and collective bargaining with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health insurance plans.
municipal-health-insurance-reform.status: The Select Board voted to accept Massachusetts General Law Chapter 32B, Sections 21 through 23, authorizing expedited collective negotiations with the Public Employee Committee over municipal health insurance plan designs. The decision aligns Southborough with Northborough and the regional school district to pursue coordinated changes to reduce premium expenses, which represent 11.2 percent of the town budget. Formal negotiations with employee representatives are expected to follow, targeting plan modifications that would take effect July 1, 2027.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Aug 11 to adopt MGL Chapter 32B, Sections 21-23, to pursue coordinated negotiations with the Public Employee Committee to reduce health insurance costs.

municipal-phone-system-upgrade.name: Municipal phone system upgrade
municipal-phone-system-upgrade.description: Capital request and transition of municipal facilities from an unsupported on-premise PBX phone system to a cloud-based solution.
